Margaret said nothing for a long time. The afternoon was warm, and a bee droned in the lavender by the gate; across the field, the men were bringing in the last of the hay. She was aware of Edward standing a little behind her, waiting, and of her own heart, which was behaving quite unreasonably. It would have been simple to say yes. He was kind, he was steady, he would never raise his voice. But she thought of the letters she had meant to write, of the town she had never seen, of all the small impossible plans she’d tucked away. “I need time,” she said at last, and her voice sounded strange to her. He nodded, and she was grateful that he did not argue.
